content.text: OI-179: ooe_redir (5a): who drives the squash's advance and flushes, and what 5a carries

OI proposes three things for OA 435 (5a), and needs OA's ruling on the first before it builds the advance. (1) ooe_rob_w's resolution flop (rd_l_cq03h, in the model's squashDue cycle) is wired straight to ooe_decrx's adv, ooe_decq's flush and ooe_rat's squash. decrx's lead comes from a new rob_w output, its resolution enable, one cycle earlier and from flops. ooe_redir then drives only FET's two channels. (2) The model queues a cycle's redirects in slot order, which makes ties deterministic at no cost. (3) 5a sends redirects and ckpt_free; the rewind beats, own_pc, held and the notices land with 5b. Built meanwhile: decq's per-slot credits (OA 435 (4)). Needs: OA

(1) The advance. OA 435 has ooe_redir raise decrx's advance. decrx takes adv_cq01h in the cycle the model's squash acts (squashDue, squash_act_lag 1), which is the cycle rob_w's rd_l_cq03h is high. decrx clocks its table from its own flop of a lead, ev_l_cq00h, which must arrive a cycle earlier, in the resolve cycle. Under the no-feedthrough rule, ooe_redir can only flop rd_l, so an advance through it lands two cycles after the model's. decq's flush and the RAT restore would then have to follow it to keep OA 428's ordering invariant (the advance no later than the flush). OI proposes that the squash's three receivers take rob_w's rd_l directly, as wires. rob_w gets one new output, rd_e_cq02h: its resolution enable (rs_en), a superset lead from its own flops, about 6 NGD by its form (to be measured). decrx widens ev_l to one lead per source (S from rob_w, one from ooe_slot) and ORs them behind its own flop. This adds no cycle and puts no logic in ccv_ooe. ooe_redir reads, per slot, decrx's flopped warp and its epoch-plus-one copy, as two new decrx outputs. It captures them in rd_l's cycle, before the advance, which is the model's rd.epoch (the epoch + 1 at resolve) even when a notice advances the same slot in that cycle. The alternative, the advance through ooe_redir, costs 2 cycles on every mispredict's squash. (2) Ordering. ooe_redir keeps at most one redirect per slot. A newer mispredict overwrites the slot's entry and takes the youngest age, as the model's supersede does. It sends the oldest entry (an S x S age matrix), ties to the lowest slot. The valid comes from a flop a cycle after rd_l and the payload a cycle later, so the model's send cycle + 2. The model orders same-cycle redirects by completion order; OI changes it to slot order so the bench compares exactly (no change in IPC; collisions are rare). (3) Fields. target_pc is zero-extended from rob_w's 48 bits to the channel's 64 (FET's PCs are 48 bits; the model's high bits are 0). In 5a, epoch_only, rewind, rewind_held, held_long and own_pc are 0. The beats need each lane's oldest unretired PC over the ROB and decq, which is rob_w slice 6's head-side scan. OI proposes they land with 5b and (7), as the notices do, unless OA wants beat inputs on ooe_redir now. ckpt_free: ooe_redir ORs the four rob_w instances' ckf_cq03h into the 16-bit mask and flops it, in the same cycle relation as the redirect's valid (A-58: a free sent with a redirect lands with it). It has a per-slot mask input from the epoch_only notice (TI-485, OA 438), tied off until 5b. Built meanwhile on oi-slot (6fc15bec, unpushed): ooe_decq's crd_cq02h, each slot's frees at an edge (its count on a flush, stale staged arrivals with it, else its take), registered beside frn and straight from flops. An assertion holds their sum to frn. decq_tb checks every slot, and the new control stale-credit-apart is caught. check-cg and check-ngd follow once the running gate frees the machine.
